tells: Names the Sheikh, states his qualification plainly, and uses 'as we do' with first-person-plural inclusion, as Author A does; the antithetical opening is close to A's 'Eyes and ears take in the surface of things, whereas inside...'
'So the believers of this verse are believers who know Allah' — Author A never opens a sentence with 'So'; would write 'The believers of this verse are thus...' or state it flatly
'Sheikh Bahmanpour puts it simply: there are two groups' — claim-colon-paraphrase with a chatty 'puts it simply'; Author A writes 'Sheikh Bahmanpour divides people into two groups'
'The Qur'an describes them repeatedly.' / 'A heart only trembles' — looser word order and emphasis than A's precise 'more than once' and 'trembles only'
'The first description is in Surah al-Anfal.' set as a one-line stub paragraph; A folds the lead-in to a verse into the close of the preceding paragraph
'about something else: catching the signs of Allah: becoming sensitive to them' — stacked double colon; Author A uses one colon and keeps the clause clean
'and he does not soften it' — a tidy closing flourish on the paragraph; Author A ends on the explanation (the gloss of shirk) and stops
'Sheikh Bahmanpour opened his course by pointing out that' — wordy reporting frame; A says 'Sheikh Bahmanpour says' or gives the claim directly
'Pursuing it means' — vague pronoun opening a passage; A names the subject ('Pursuing ʿirfan')
Plain declarative exposition, paragraph two picks up the first ('The other prayers have their own times'), and the characteristic comma before a paired 'or' ('every night, or every other night')
Short declaratives, Sheikh named and paraphrased then quoted, A's paired-comma habit ('the future, or the past', 'hear, and see'), and the paragraph ends on the gloss of shirk without a flourish

Quotation introduced by name and then spoken to, A's paired-comma habit ('obeys, and acts righteously'), and the recap uses A's chapter vocabulary (receiver rusted, can be repaired, reflect, know, listen, and reason)
'The reward.' — verbless fragment used as a signpost; Author A writes full sentences and lets the paragraph opening carry the link
'is in the lecturer's reading a clean life' — Author A always names him ('Sheikh Bahmanpour reads it as'); never 'the lecturer'
'The second gift is a different kind of life.' / 'The third gift is peace.' tacked onto the end of paragraphs as teasers; A opens the next step at the head of a paragraph
'rise above the concerns that infect everyone else' — slightly dramatic diction compared with A's sober paraphrase
Quotations introduced by name with a plain reporting verb and woven into A's own sentence; restrained register; no flourish at paragraph end

Opens by picking up the previous point ('rests on the same humility'), second paragraph links back ('God's invitation to recite these words'), paired-comma habit ('above our level, and beyond our capacity')
Paragraph opens by picking up the last step ('If the faculty can be repaired'), Sheikh named, verse lead-in closes the paragraph as in the reference, 'thus' rather than an opening 'So'
Quotation introduced and then explained ('What the prayer asks to lose is...'), back-reference to Chapter One, and A's paired-comma habit ('the people, and the work', 'household, or the marketplace')
Each quotation is set up and then spoken to; 'For some of us' first-person-plural inclusion as in the reference; paired-comma habit ('chosen for His nearness, and granted the sight of His face')
